PullRequest.Title: Create custom CodeQL workflow
PullRequest.Body:
Added custom `CodeQL` workflow.
Updated `CodeQL` config file to only include production code.
Removed unnecessary `CodeQL` artifacts.
Disabled `CodeQL` injection in some utility pipelines.
Removed test code dependency from `taskProvider.ts`.

This reduces `CodeQL` CI time from `20-25 mins` to `10-13 mins` and will likely reduce it further once the cache is applied.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub CodeQL analysis on pull requests, main/release pushes, and the weekly schedule
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each workflow run must complete checkout, CodeQL initialization, and analysis for its matrix language before the CodeQL job completes; this is CI-only and not on an editor product path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout the repository and obtain CodeQL action/dependency data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per language job, so two checkout/init sequences per workflow run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No repository-defined advanced CodeQL workflow existed in the base diff; CodeQL was supplied externally/default setup, so exact prior boundary cardinality is not represented in repository files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both matrix jobs must finish for the workflow to complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One analysis per configured language per workflow run, two analyses total.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The PR replaces externally configured/default analysis with a custom workflow and substantially expands paths-ignore; available repository evidence does not show an increased analysis cardinality or hotter trigger path versus that prior setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the dominant CPU/I/O work of the CodeQL workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Repository source size after paths-ignore filtering, with two matrix entries: JavaScript/TypeScript and Rust.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two language matrix jobs may run in parallel; fail-fast is disabled. Each language performs one checkout, one initialization, and one analysis.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CodeQL dependency caching is enabled. Cold runs may populate/download dependencies; warm runs can reuse the action cache. The source filtering is static and has no application cache lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the new workflow's two-job boundary and trigger model; insufficient evidence that it regresses performance relative to the external default setup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact default-setup triggers, runner cache hit rate, and prior analysis duration are external to the repository. The diff and PR context indicate replacement and scope reduction, not additive application work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The workflow adds explicit CI boundaries but is designed to replace default setup and narrows analyzed paths; there is no high-confidence diff evidence of duplicated or increased work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Azure dependency-check, type-publishing, and Copilot asset-update pipelines
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pipeline startup and configured build/publish steps remain the critical path; auto-injected CodeQL work is explicitly disabled.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pipeline execution for each utility workflow invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged by this diff; the new variables suppress an injected analysis task rather than adding parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior is changed by these hunks.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that these changes remove rather than add CI work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact duration saved by suppressing external task injection is not present in repository evidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; the changed variables reduce external analysis overhead.

Scenarios.Scenario: TypeScript task auto-detection when VS Code requests contributed TypeScript tasks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: provideTasks waits concurrently for active-file projectInfo and one workspace-wide findFiles call, then checks discovered config URIs and builds task definitions. Workspace search remains bounded by the same five-second timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search the workspace for tsconfig*.json through vscode.workspace.findFiles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One workspace-wide search per provideTasks invocation, regardless of the number of matching configs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the same getConfigsForWorkspace call raced a five-second wait and cancellation callback; the boundary count and timeout were identical.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Task enumeration waits for this search unless it reaches the unchanged five-second timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check existence of candidate tsconfig files and local tsc executables.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existence checks scale with discovered configs, with two possible local-tsc checks per distinct project.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These checks occur after config discovery before task results are returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request projectInfo from the TypeScript server for the active TypeScript editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per provideTasks invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with workspace config discovery and is bounded by the existing two-second race.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of workspace tsconfig files after the single workspace search; existence checks and task construction scale with distinct config paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Active-file lookup and workspace search run in parallel. Config existence checks use Promise.all. The workspace search itself is one coalesced VS Code findFiles request, not one request per config.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is introduced or bypassed. Each provider invocation performs the existing workspace search; cancellation terminates a timed-out search. The new raceTimeout also clears its timer when the search completes early.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct call path and helper implementation that the new code does not add work; it removes the dependency on test utilities and clears the timer on early completion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual workspace search duration and config count vary by workspace, but the changed helper preserves both boundary cardinality and the timeout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Before and after both perform one bounded workspace search; the replacement preserves cancellation semantics and improves timer cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Packaging and loading built-in Markdown and TypeScript language extensions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Packaging filters determine shipped files; extension activation loads the TypeScript task provider and its imported utility modules.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One packaging traversal per extension build; the scripts subtree is now excluded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Scripts were previously eligible for packaging; the changed ignore rule removes them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This reduces packaging input and shipped bytes rather than adding work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load task-provider module dependencies during TypeScript extension activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per extension host module load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior task provider imported testUtils, which itself imported assertion and filesystem modules; the changed import narrows the module graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff replaces an import from a broad test utility module with the existing focused async helper.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Packaged file count/bytes and imported module graph at extension activation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency or fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence these edits remove packaging/module-load work; no regression mechanism is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No package-size or activation benchmark is present, so the size of the improvement is not quantified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; both changes reduce eager packaging or module-load scope.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all nine changed files and the performance-sensitive paths. The custom CodeQL workflow and Azure variables move/reduce CI analysis work, packaging ignores reduce shipped inputs, and the runtime timeout replacement preserves the single five-second-bounded workspace search while improving timer cleanup. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
